message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or your local tenant‑rights organization.) | Category | What the law says | Practical Tips | |----------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions (repairs, cleaning, unpaid rent). | • Get a written receipt and keep a copy of the lease.
• Take photos of the unit before moving in and after moving out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity).
• Repairs must be made within a reasonable time after notice. | • Report problems in writing (email or text) and keep a copy.
• If repairs are not made, you may withhold rent or repair and deduct, but do so carefully and document everything. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable. | • Keep records of all payments (bank statements, receipts). | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hrs) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Ask for a written notice of entry. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must give notice of non‑renewal at least **30 days** before the lease ends. | • Provide written notice and keep a copy. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the court‑ordered eviction process (notice, filing, hearing).
• Common grounds: non‑payment of rent, lease violations, or landlord’s own need for the property. | • Respond promptly to any notices.
• If you believe the eviction is unlawful, seek legal help immediately. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Document any disturbances and notify the landlord in writing. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major problem, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but you must follow the proper procedure (written notice, reasonable cost, etc.). | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Subletting** | • The lease may prohibit subletting; if it does, you need the landlord’s written permission. | • Always get written approval before subletting. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify who pays utilities. | • Verify utility responsibilities in writing. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas has several tenant‑rights groups (e.g., Texas Tenants Union, local legal aid). | • Contact them for help with disputes or eviction defense. | ### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Read the lease thoroughly** – note rent amount, due date, security deposit, pet policy, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document the condition** – take dated photos or video of each room, appliances, and any existing damage. 3. **Get a written receipt** for the security deposit and any initial rent payment. 4. **Ask for a copy of the lease** in a format you can keep (PDF or printed). ### When Problems Arise - **Write a formal notice** to the landlord describing the issue and requesting repair. - **Keep copies** of all correspondence. - **If the landlord fails to act**, you may: - Withhold rent (but only after following the proper procedure). - Repair the issue yourself and deduct the cost (again, follow the correct steps). - File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if discrimination is suspected. - Seek legal counsel or mediation. --- #### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 92 (Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law). - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – [https://www.tchra.texas.gov](https://www.tchra.texas.gov) - **Texas Tenants Union** – [https://www.texastenantsunion.org](https://www.texastenantsunion.org) - **Legal Aid of North Texas** – [https://www.lantex.org](https://www.lantex.org) Feel free to ask if you need more detail on any specific point!
